description: At the close of 2025, 42.2% of people deprived of liberty in Mexico were without a sentence: of 231,436 people in prison, 97,722 had no judicial resolution, and of those, 50.1% were under prisión preventiva oficiosa (INEGI Censo Nacional del Sistema Penitenciario 2026).
energy_note: Ninety-seven thousand people, not convicted of anything.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the sex split, which runs against the usual direction
description: Among the unsentenced, 34.5% of men and 31.5% of women were in justified preventive detention, while 49.7% of men and 55.2% of women were under PPO. Automatic detention falls proportionally harder on women; the absolute numbers are overwhelmingly men.
energy_note: Proportionally worse for women, numerically almost all men.

aspect: EXAMPLE - two states apply it to everyone
description: Estado de México and Michoacán reported that 100% of their unsentenced prison population was under prisión preventiva oficiosa - 12,349 people and 3,044 people respectively.
energy_note: One hundred per cent, in two states.

description: PPO entered the Constitution in 2008; a later reform to Article 19 expanded the list of qualifying offences to include extortion, false tax receipts, fuel theft and fentanyl-related crimes. The prison population rose from 235,197 at end-2024 to 256,127 at end-2025.
energy_note: Every expansion of the list fills more cells.

aspect: It is punishment that precedes the finding
description: A man accused of a listed offence is imprisoned from the start of proceedings without a judge analysing his individual case, even absent solid evidence or any procedural risk. If acquitted years later, the years are simply gone.
energy_note: Acquitted in 2029, having been in prison since 2025.

aspect: Waiting in prison changes the plea
description: Where the wait for trial exceeds the likely sentence, pleading guilty is the faster route out - so PPO manufactures convictions independently of guilt, which is the mechanism behind POL-001's 20% who pleaded guilty.
energy_note: Confessing because it is quicker than being innocent.
